extracted.intended_audience: registered patent and trademark practitioners before the USPTO (including firm managing partners and trademark practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and obligations for practitioners handling USPTO trademark filings, with emphasis on signature rules, competent representation, supervision of staff, and disciplinary consequences. Includes mitigation/remediation behaviors that affect sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO trademark signature rule (TMEP §611.01(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The named signatory must be the person who enters his or her electronic signature on a trademark document presented to the Office (TMEP §611.01(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order emphasizes that the trademark signature rule is a substantive rule, not a mere 'technical' requirement, and that failure of the named signatory to enter his or her signature may actually or potentially harm the intellectual property rights of applicants and registrants and the integrity of the USPTO trademark registration process. The decision cites approximately 690 trademark documents filed over ~33 months with impermissible signatures as the factual example of the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must provide competent representation to a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence includes adequately understanding USPTO trademark signature rules and relevant TMEP guidance. The Final Order identifies representing clients before the Office without such understanding and presenting trademark documents that violated signature rules as examples of incompetence. The USPTO publishes the TMEP and trademark guidance (tmep.uspto.gov; www.uspto.gov/trademarks) which practitioners are expected to consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to ensure compliance with signature rules and to promptly address improperly filed documents can violate this duty. The respondent's prompt communication to clients and actions after learning of the violations are cited as relevant remedial conduct under this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner/supervisory responsibilities (37 C.F.R. § 11.501(b) and § 11.503(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is a partner in a law firm must make reasonable efforts to ensure the firm has measures giving reasonable assurance that all practitioners and non-practitioner assistants conform to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. § 11.501(b); § 11.503(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As managing partner with managerial authority, a practitioner is responsible for ensuring trademark attorneys and non-attorney trademark assistants comply with USPTO rules. The Final Order treats failure to ensure compliance (allowing assistants to enter signatures) as a breach of these supervisory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misrepresentation to the Office (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not engage in misrepresentation; presenting documents to the USPTO where the practitioner knows the named signatory did not sign constitutes misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will view submission of trademark documents (including declarations) with impermissible signatures as misrepresentation when the filer knew the named signatory had not signed and knew the Office would rely on the documents as part of the registration process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to the integrity of the trademark system (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not engage in conduct prejudicial to the integrity of the U.S. trademark registration system (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting multiple trademark documents with impermissible signatures is identified as conduct that prejudices the integrity of the registration system because it may adversely affect applicants' and registrants' rights and the Office's reliance on filed materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and consultation of USPTO/TMEP guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners should consult USPTO-published trademark guidance, including the Trademark Manual of Examining Procedure (TMEP) and the USPTO trademarks webpages, to ensure competent practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes the agency 'has published ample, readily available information' and specifically references the TMEP (tmep.uspto.gov) and USPTO trademark pages (www.uspto.gov/trademarks) as resources practitioners should use to understand rules such as signature requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation, client communication, and cooperation as mitigating factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly informing affected clients, working to remediate filings, taking corrective action at no charge, and cooperating with OED investigation can mitigate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent directly contacted affected clients about impermissible signatures, contacted the USPTO regarding filings made in violation of signature requirements, continued to work with clients about potential harm, and fully cooperated with OED (including candid interviews). The Order cites contrition, acceptance of responsibility, and cooperation as considerations in imposing a public reprimand and probation rather than harsher discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary remedies and enforcement procedures (reprimand, probation, suspension process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose public reprimand, probation, and suspension; OED may issue an Order to Show Cause and request USPTO Director suspend a practitioner for specified violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this settlement the agreed sanctions include a public reprimand and twelve-month probation. If the OED Director believes the practitioner fails to comply during probation, OED will issue an Order to Show Cause, give 15 days to respond, and may request the USPTO Director enter an immediate suspension for up to four months. The Order also preserves OED's ability to seek separate discipline for misconduct underlying an Order to Show Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and precedent use of disciplinary records
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders and disciplinary decisions are published and may be considered in future proceedings concerning the same or similar misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED will publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and a notice in the Official Gazette. The record may be considered by the Office in addressing future complaints or as an aggravating factor in subsequent discipline or to rebut representations by the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement terms may include waiver of review/appeal rights and allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of a settlement, a practitioner may waive rights to seek reconsideration, have the Final Order reviewed, or otherwise appeal, and the parties may each bear their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent agreed to waive rights under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.56 and 11.57 and waived other appeals; each party bears their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the Agreement and Final Order.
